      "observations": [
        "All 287 owned diff lines across five paths were read. The command module gains a fourth supported argument, its own callback map and function-or-Boolean support lookup. The Address Book moves its cards-table focus guard into support while leaving selectedCards length and mailing-list exclusion in enablement. The subject's no-contact wording is broader than the actual predicate: a focused empty list still claims support but is disabled; an unfocused list declines support even if contacts remain selected.",
        "The new registration preserves the explicit cardsPane?.cardsList guard before comparing document.activeElement with the table body. The proposed single optional-chain comparison is not adopted. A nullish left/right comparison can differ from the guarded expression under loose equality, but no claim is made that an uninitialized list and null activeElement are reachable together in this UI.",
        "The command module, Address Book callback registration and shared globalOverlay.js are byte-identical between this landing and the fixed accepted revision. The checked comm overlay already searches top.controllers when the dispatcher's first supported controller is disabled; its comment states that this is not the same controller set as the dispatcher. Native dispatcher/edit-menu/keyboard internals remain a bounded unpaired dependency. The bug's failure rationale is not treated as proof that every comm caller stops after a disabled handler.",
        "Actual selectedCards maps selected row indices to cards. copySelected still concatenates vCards and assigns the same supports-string to text/vcard and text/plain; the existing clipboard lesson is reused. doCommand checks enablement but does not independently check support, so support is a lookup contract rather than an extra guard on direct method calls.",
        "The new details-pane scenario blurs the cards table, selects the contact name, calls copyByEditMenu, then selects the primary email and calls copyByKeyboard. Its two direct equalities check the clipboard text. The shared menu helper uses window.goDoCommand on macOS and actual Edit-menu activation elsewhere; keyboard uses accel+C. This does not directly assert which native controller was selected, a macOS native-menu click, all focus transitions or rendered accessibility behavior.",
        "The affected test_copy task now calls shared helpers for menu, one-card accelerator and multi-card accelerator paths; existing content/flavor equality and no-selection/mailing-list command checks remain. Newly added Assert.equal(copiedName, \"basic person\") and Assert.equal(copiedEmail, \"basic@invalid\") omit message arguments. The extracted shared Assert.ok(!copyMenuItem.disabled) also has no message and retains that omission in accepted source. Existing neighboring message-less assertions are distinguished from these added/extracted sites; missing should alone is not the finding.",
        "The helper comments describe menu/keyboard actions and the macOS substitution, but @returns {*} does not state the async completion contract. Its body awaits clipboard data of the requested flavor. A clearer local JSDoc suggestion is to state that completion supplies the copied data and can reject on the wait's failure, without inventing a native clipboard type or changing unrelated comments. Setup, action and checks are grouped locally; the new supported callback remains a simple return and the dispatch method preserves its early disabled guard.",
        "Complete retained primary current comments 0–5, activity and ending controls were read. The initial macOS report and Linux confirmation concern selecting displayed contact text, without editing. The author's query-timing explanation is explicitly tentative; the later first-supporting-controller explanation is historical rationale, checked against the exact adopted registration and bounded comm lookup rather than treated as a universal runtime result.",
        "The complete own review's two actual inline bodies and optional-chaining replacement were read. The reviewer proposes a single comparison; the author keeps the separate cards-list guard because both compared values can be falsy, while explicitly uncertain whether that state occurs here. Actual owned and accepted source retain the guard. Acceptance and Not Done badges do not prove the proposed expression equivalent.",
        "The exact source checks preserve the narrower implementation boundary: support depends on cards-table focus, while enablement depends on nonempty non-list selection. The new direct clipboard assertions and extracted helper's missing messages are recorded as scoped manual-review findings. Native dispatcher behavior, platform copy routing and the linked regression ranges remain bounded unread dependencies, with no new runtime result."
